topics.topic_label: Frontier safety oversight (a validity audit finds an 'always positive' policy scoring 0.690 on R-Judge, above five models that genuinely discriminate, and three broad benchmarks ranking the same 18 models differently; Pacing the Frontier lands with 1,324 frontier-lab employees asking governments to deliberately slow automated AI research)

Content provenance & training-data copyright (EU AI Act Article 50 becomes applicable and California's SB 942 becomes operative on the same calendar day, by design; ~190 organisations sign the Code of Practice on Transparency, with Lufthansa, Getty Images, Lenovo and Bulgari among the deployers)

EU AI Act (Article 50 applies from 2 August and the Commission opens a complaints tool, a whistleblower tool and a downstream-GPAI channel, with ceilings of €35M/7% and €15M/3%; systems already on the market get until 2 December 2026 for machine-readable marking; three widely-shared LinkedIn posts give three incompatible accounts)

Frontier safety oversight (the White House met its 1 August deadline for a frontier-evaluation framework and will not say what is in it, who has seen it, or when labs start using it; labs review it behind closed doors on Tuesday; a safety trilemma proof says capability, reliable safety and open access cannot coexist)

Frontier safety oversight (EO 14409's 1 August deliverables — classified benchmarking with NSA/CISA/NIST, a voluntary frontier disclosure framework, an OPM cyber workforce plan — produced nothing public; meanwhile a voluntary safety-evaluation framework is circulating privately to leading labs)

Content provenance & copyright (~190 organisations signed the transparency Code of Practice, 83 to Section 1 and 152 to Section 2, so the marking format gets settled in September task forces rather than in national court; on HN the argument has moved from 'is AI art good' to whether publishing it signals you are wasting the reader's time, with explicit calls for social enforcement)

Content provenance & copyright (Article 50 is being enforced since 2 August — chatbots must disclose, deepfakes must be labelled, generated content must carry machine-readable marks — and the two best pieces of the day both separate human-facing disclosure from machine-verifiable provenance instead of collapsing them into 'label your AI'; on HN the reader-side enforcement is already running, with AI hero images read as a costly-signalling failure at 772 points)

Content provenance & copyright (Article 50 went live on 2 August so AI-generated or manipulated content must carry machine-readable labels - and on the same front page TIME is caught serving AI crawlers a different site with advertising embedded in the text models ingest, Meta ran ads containing AI-generated CSAM, and Grokipedia is found to have silently stopped reviewing edits in April while still presenting as live)

Content provenance & training-data copyright (Oracle bars AI-generated code from OpenJDK, read on HN as legal positioning — Oracle wants to preserve its ability to sue over AI-washed proprietary code, which it cannot do while accepting unprovenanced AI contributions; the EU AI Act's machine-readable content-marking duty is now operative and is an engineering task, not a legal one)
